title: the pact with Sugriva
hook: a bundle of jewels, and a brother-in-law who only knows the anklets

segments.voice: Yesterday: Rama and Sugriva swore friendship around a fire. Two exiles on one branch.

Sugriva has something to show Rama. A while ago, he says, five of us were sitting up here, and we saw a rakshasa flying across the sky carrying a woman. She was crying out: Rama, Lakshmana. When she saw us below, she dropped her upper cloth and some of her jewelry, tied in a bundle. We kept them safe. He sends someone into the cave to bring them out.
screen: `FIVE OF US, ON THE MOUNTAIN.` → `A WOMAN CRYING OUT.` → `A BUNDLE DROPPED.`

segments.voice: Rama sees the cloth and the ornaments and breaks down. He presses them to his chest and weeps. Sita did more than call out. She left a trail. Passing over five strangers on a mountain, she threw down what she could, hoping someone would get it to Rama. And someone did. Then Rama turns to Lakshmana: do you know these? Lakshmana's answer is not what you'd expect. I don't know her armlets, he says. I don't know her earrings. But I know the anklets, because I bowed at her feet every day. Through all the years in the forest, Lakshmana kept his eyes lowered before his brother's wife. He looked at her feet, because that's where you look when you bow to someone you honor, an elder, a mother. In many Indian families, touching an elder's feet is an everyday sign of respect, and this verse is often quoted to show what that respect can mean. Then the pact becomes real. Rama asks: who is he? Where did he take her? Sugriva admits he doesn't know where Ravana lives. But he promises he'll find out, and that Rama will have Sita back. Rama, still holding the jewelry, asks him to begin. A friendship sworn before the fire now has something to hold in its hands.
screen: `SITA LEFT A TRAIL.` · `I KNOW ONLY THE ANKLETS.` · `EYES LOWERED, IN RESPECT.` · `THE PACT HAS SOMETHING TO HOLD.`

segments.voice: Let your gaze drop softly to your own feet. Breathe in and think of someone you honor, a parent, a teacher, an elder; breathe out and offer them, silently, the respect of a bow. Keep your eyes low, your breath slow, and that person in mind.
Nupura, an anklet: the one ornament Lakshmana recognizes among Sita's jewels, because he bowed at her feet every day.
Your line: I know only the anklets. Respect can be as quiet as lowered eyes. That's day five hundred eighty-four.

howItsDone: Touching the feet of parents, teachers and elders (pranam or charan sparsh) is a common gesture of respect in many Hindu families, and Lakshmana's words about the anklets are often quoted when it's explained.

original.note: Sanskrit nūpura: an anklet. the one ornament Lakshmana recognizes.

trapdoor: what you thought: Lakshmana just has a poor memory for jewelry.
what it means: he kept his eyes lowered before Sita, out of respect.
what a scholar hears: Kishkindha 6 has the well-known verse naming keyūra (armlets), kuṇḍala (earrings) and nūpura (anklets), seen 'from daily bowing at her feet'.
